invariants: Actual HTTP initialize/initialized/list/call fields, selected protocol/session/header fields, JSON/batched JSON, POST SSE and GET notifications match the sixteen original factory/SDK observations at declared GET/cancellation admission barriers.
Peer MCP errors, HTTP 401, unexpected or missing content types and invalid envelopes reject with the observed error fields; no transport can invent successful tools or output.
Cancel and timeout settle without awaiting the cancellation HTTP acknowledgment; close reclaims every owned send, stream/retry task, writer and pending request.
Close does not silently DELETE a server session; explicit termination uses the current session/protocol headers and accepts the original 405 outcome.
The actual embedded Python/ToolsService consumer executes the advertised HTTP tool and withdraws it on awaited scope unload.
identity: One protocol client with correlated requests, optional server session id and owned HTTP/SSE resources; fresh GET/cancel admission barriers are explicit observer inputs.
ownership: The client owns network writers, send and stream/retry tasks, pending requests and close; the caller owns explicit headers and cancellation, and the observer owns its controlled peer process.
ordering: Initialization and negotiated version precede initialized notification and tool publication; observed optional GET admission precedes list, and cancellation admission precedes observer shutdown. These barriers do not certify an ordering between unconstrained concurrent HTTP requests.
errors: Selected original factory/SDK error name, message, code and absent-versus-null data are retained; malformed URL factory failure stops at the original five-second close barrier instead of inventing a retry generation.
cancellation: Cancellation dispatch is owned asynchronously, a stalled notification acknowledgment cannot hold the canceled request, and shutdown drains owned work and closes or aborts writers.
adaptation: Python 3.8 standard-library asyncio streams and TLS primitives; no Node or third-party HTTP runtime in the product. The Windows controlled TCP-only observer uses Selector policy to avoid its separate Proactor accept/stop race; product clients keep the normal runtime policy.
open_questions: Bounded clean receipt-bound acceptance at 8a17485d passed for the sixteen selected source/SDK/native rows and actual extracted ToolsService consumer. This is not complete SDK HTTP parity. TLS/redirect/compression/encoding/WHATWG URL equivalence, resumable SSE/replay and retry exhaustion, disposal during factory rejection, ACP mounting and Win7 remain unaccepted. Preserved browser startup cancellation, Proactor warning and HTTP 10054 diagnostics remain open; the passing clean gate is not a root-cause fix.

rc1_review.scope: Current finite executable provider/consumer corpora, original-browser and extracted observations in the single full receipt. Historical alpha evidence remains historical; no inventory-wide parity, arbitrary ABI/history, paid-provider or Win7 certification.
